$comment: Previously https://torus.dev/schemas/restricted-reference.schema.json. Renamespaced 2026-09-01 to the canonical torusai.io namespace. Nothing resolves schemas by $id — every validator loads by file path — so the change is declarative. Enforced by torus-multibuild lib/namespace.mjs.
title: Restricted reference
description: Metadata ABOUT an externally held artifact. The Library records where something lives, who controls it, and how to request it — never the artifact and never a credential. Fields that could carry secret material are validated by engine/src/diligence/secrets.js.

id.description: A Library ID, so a reference is addressable exactly like a paper.

owner.description: Role or function accountable for the artifact. A role is preferred to a person.

custodian.description: Who or what holds the artifact — the party to ask. Never a credential.

storage.description: Where the artifact lives. A locator, never an access path with embedded credentials.

locator.description: A human-resolvable pointer (a path, a case number, a folder name). Must not be a pre-authenticated or signed URL.

classification.description: Sensitivity label from the instance's configured vocabulary.

audience.description: Audience of the REFERENCE itself. Defaults to the most restrictive configured audience when omitted — never widened.

retention.description: Retention category. The Library never deletes canon; this records the custodian's obligation.

diligence_categories.description: Categories from the instance's configured diligence taxonomy.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the external artifact, supplied by the custodian. Lets the Library prove which version was referenced without holding the artifact.

status.description: Same lifecycle as a paper — references are chronicle records too.

access_notes.description: How to request access, in prose. MUST NOT contain credentials of any kind; validated.
